vocabulary.definition: Hypertext Transfer Protocol: application protocol used for transferring requests and responses on the web and in many APIs.
HTTP defines GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE as safe methods because their defined semantics are essentially read-only.
HTTP defines a method as idempotent when multiple identical requests are intended to have the same effect as one such request; PUT, DELETE, and safe methods are idempotent by specification.
The HTTP GET method requests transfer of a current selected representation of the target resource.
HTTP HEAD is identical to GET except the server must not send content in the response.
HTTP POST asks the target resource to process the enclosed representation according to the resource-specific semantics.
